cdif.bbr.metadata.cdifDataType.objectRef.description: A reference to a node defined elsewhere, by its @id.

cdif.bbr.metadata.odrlProperties.odrlOff.title: ODRL Offer
cdif.bbr.metadata.odrlProperties.odrlOff.description:
CDIF Access profile of an ODRL 2.2 Offer (https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-model/#policy-offer): the baseline access and usage conditions a data provider sets for a digital object, without naming who they apply to (that is an ODRL Agreement). Built on the generic odrlPolicy block, which carries the ODRL structure; this block adds only CDIF's own rules. Draft from the CDIF Access spreadsheet (CDIF_Access_Profile_ODRL_Classes_Properties_Description.xlsx) and the cdifbook data_access chapter.
Keys carry the odrl: prefix and the document's @context declares the odrl, cdifa1 (https://w3id.org/cdif/access/profile1/), rdf and xsd prefixes. The ODRL JSON-LD context is not used, so nothing coerces a string to an IRI: every IRI value (target, action, parties, operands) is an {"@id": ...} object.
An access condition (something done BEFORE the digital object is retrieved) is a permission duty constrained by odrl:event odrl:lt odrl:policyUsage (https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-model/#duty-perm). Everything else is a usage condition: a permission (may do), an obligation (must do) or a prohibition (must not do).
OPEN QUESTIONS are marked "OPEN:" below.

@context.description: JSON-LD namespace prefixes for ODRL policy properties. Not required: an Offer embedded in a CDIF record inherits the record's @context.

@id.description: Globally unique, resolvable IRI for this Offer (the spreadsheet's uid). A resolver should be able to return application/ld+json, not only an HTML page.

odrl:profile.description: The CDIF Access ODRL profile this policy uses, which supplies the cdifa1: actions the ODRL core vocabulary lacks (download, assent, datadestruction, ...). OPEN: nothing is published at this IRI yet, and it names a .ttl file where ODRL expects a profile identifier. The cdifa1: form is accepted because compaction under the cdifa1 prefix rewrites the full IRI to it.

odrl:target.description: Asset all rules apply to, if given once at policy level (range odrl:Asset).

odrl:assigner.description: The party issuing the Offer, normally the repository or data custodian, given once at policy level (range odrl:Party). ODRL also accepts an assigner on every rule instead; CDIF asks for the policy-level form. The spreadsheet does not list an assigner yet.

odrl:assignee.description: Party all rules apply to, if given once at policy level (range odrl:Party).

odrl:permission.description: Actions a user may perform on the target (usage conditions).

odrl:target.description: The asset, normally a distribution or data service (range odrl:Asset).

odrl:output.description: An asset created by exercising the action (range odrl:Asset).

odrl:action.description: The permitted action (range odrl:Action). OPEN: the cdifa1 action vocabulary is not defined, so values are not enumerated; whether it is an ODRL profile or a standalone controlled vocabulary is still to be settled.

odrl:assigner.description: Party granting this permission, if not given at policy level (range odrl:Party).

odrl:assignee.description: Who may exercise the permission (range odrl:Party), as a party or a (refined) PartyCollection, e.g. registered users located in the UK. This is the book's form; the spreadsheet scopes users with odrl:constraint instead. OPEN: settle on one, or say when each is used.

odrl:constraint.description: Conditions on exercising the permission (range odrl:Constraint), e.g. only users located in the UK (the spreadsheet's way of scoping users; see odrl:assignee).

odrl:duty.description: Access conditions (range odrl:Duty): actions that must be completed before the permitted action, e.g. assent to an End User Licence before download.

odrl:obligation.description: Actions every user of the target must perform (range odrl:Duty), e.g. destroy the data at the end of a project. The spreadsheet gives 1..*; drafted as 0..* because an Offer with only permissions is common. OPEN: confirm.

odrl:prohibition.description: Actions a user must not perform (range odrl:Prohibition), e.g. share TRE credentials.

odrl:output.description: An asset created by exercising the action (range odrl:Asset).

odrl:assigner.description: Party issuing this prohibition, if not given at policy level (range odrl:Party).

odrl:assignee.description: Who the prohibition applies to (range odrl:Party).

odrl:constraint.description: Conditions under which the prohibition applies (range odrl:Constraint).

odrl:remedy.description: Duties owed if the prohibition is infringed (range odrl:Duty).

accessConditionMarker.description: The constraint odrl:event odrl:lt odrl:policyUsage: the duty must be fulfilled before the permission is exercised. In CDIF Access this is what marks a duty as an access condition. Each operand accepts the odrl: compact IRI and the full IRI.

AccessCondition.description: A permission duty carrying the accessConditionMarker. The spreadsheet gives the duty action as 1..*; ODRL allows one action per rule, so several pre-conditions are several duties. OPEN: the spreadsheet does not say what an assent duty assents to (e.g. which licence document); a duty target is one candidate. OPEN: the spreadsheet lists constraint @type with cardinality 1 but gives no value and omits it on this constraint, so it is optional.

odrl:action.description: The action to complete first, e.g. cdifa1:assent (range odrl:Action).

cdif.bbr.metadata.odrlProperties.odrlPol.title: ODRL Policy
cdif.bbr.metadata.odrlProperties.odrlPol.description: An ODRL 2.2 Policy (https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-model/#policy): a group of permissions, prohibitions and obligations, typed by one of its subclasses: Set (the default), Offer, Agreement, Request, Ticket, Assertion or Privacy. A target or party given at policy level applies to every rule (https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-model/#composition), so each subclass requirement below is met by the policy-level property or by that property on every rule concerned. The subclass requirements are those stated in the ODRL vocabulary (https://www.w3.org/ns/odrl/2/ODRL22.ttl); requirements on meaning (e.g. an Offer grants no privileges to an assignee) cannot be checked by a schema.

@context.description: JSON-LD namespace prefixes for ODRL properties.

@id.description: Globally unique IRI for the policy (ODRL uid).

odrl:profile.description: ODRL profiles the policy conforms to.

odrl:inheritFrom.description: Parent policies whose rules this policy inherits.

allOf.description: The rules must include a duty describing obligations on the use of personal information.

hasTarget.description: A target at policy level, or on every rule.

hasAssigner.description: An assigner at policy level, or on every permission and prohibition.

hasAssignee.description: An assignee at policy level, or on every permission and prohibition.

noAssignee.description: A Ticket names no assignee; it is granted to whoever holds it.

cdif.bbr.metadata.odrlProperties.odrlRul.title: ODRL Rule
cdif.bbr.metadata.odrlProperties.odrlRul.description: An ODRL 2.2 Rule (https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-model/#rule): a Permission (may do), a Prohibition (must not do) or a Duty (must do). Every rule has one action and may name its target asset, the parties (assigner, assignee) and constraints. Target and parties may instead be given once at policy level (odrlPolicy), so only the action is required here. A Permission may carry duties that must be fulfilled to exercise it, a Prohibition remedies owed if it is broken, and a Duty consequences owed if it is not fulfilled.

@context.description: JSON-LD namespace prefixes for ODRL properties.

Target.description: The asset, as a reference or an Asset or AssetCollection node.

PartyRef.description: A party, as a reference or a Party or PartyCollection node.

odrl:output.description: An asset created by exercising the action, e.g. the result of odrl:derive.

odrl:duty.description: Duties that must be fulfilled before the permission can be exercised.

odrl:remedy.description: Duties owed if the prohibition is infringed.

odrl:consequence.description: Further duties owed if this duty is not fulfilled.

cdif.bbr.metadata.odrlProperties.odrlAct.title: ODRL Action
cdif.bbr.metadata.odrlProperties.odrlAct.description: An ODRL 2.2 Action (https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-model/#action) as used in a rule: either a reference to the action ({"@id": "odrl:use"}), or, when the action itself is narrowed, an object holding the action in rdf:value plus odrl:refinement constraints (e.g. print, at most 1200 dpi). Actions are open IRIs (odrlTerms), so ODRL profile actions validate.

@context.description: JSON-LD namespace prefixes for ODRL properties.

cdif.bbr.metadata.odrlProperties.odrlCon.title: ODRL Constraint
cdif.bbr.metadata.odrlProperties.odrlCon.description: An ODRL 2.2 Constraint (https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-model/#constraint) or LogicalConstraint (https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-model/#constraint-logical). A Constraint compares a left operand with a right operand using an operator, e.g. odrl:spatial odrl:eq <country>. A LogicalConstraint combines constraints with exactly one of odrl:and, odrl:or, odrl:xone or odrl:andSequence. Operands and operators are open IRIs (odrlTerms), so ODRL profile terms validate.

@context.description: JSON-LD namespace prefixes for ODRL properties.

@id.description: Optional; needed when a LogicalConstraint refers to this constraint by reference.

odrl:rightOperand.description: A literal, a value object ({"@value", "@type"}) or an {@id} reference.

odrl:rightOperandReference.description: An IRI whose dereferenced value is the right operand.

odrl:dataType.description: Datatype of the right operand, e.g. xsd:decimal.

odrl:unit.description: Unit of the right operand, e.g. a currency or unit of measure.

odrl:status.description: The current value of the left operand, for comparison with the right operand.

odrl:and.description: All of the constraints must be satisfied.

odrl:or.description: At least one of the constraints must be satisfied.

odrl:xone.description: Exactly one of the constraints must be satisfied.

odrl:andSequence.description: All of the constraints must be satisfied, in order.

constraintList.description: The operand constraints, as an RDF list ({"@list": [...]}), each inline or an {@id} reference.

cdif.bbr.metadata.cdifDataType.objectRef.title: Object Reference
cdif.bbr.metadata.cdifDataType.objectRef.description: A reference to a node defined elsewhere, by its @id.

cdif.bbr.metadata.odrlProperties.odrlTer.title: ODRL Terms
cdif.bbr.metadata.odrlProperties.odrlTer.description: Type library of references to ODRL 2.2 vocabulary terms (https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-vocab/): actions, left operands, operators, right operands and conflict strategies. Generated from https://www.w3.org/ns/odrl/2/ODRL22.ttl, excluding terms marked deprecated. Actions and operands are open, because ODRL profiles extend them; conflict terms are closed. Each term is an {"@id": ...} reference, compact (odrl:use) or full IRI.

Action.description: Reference to an ODRL Action action. Open: any IRI is accepted, so ODRL profile terms (e.g. cdifa1:) validate; the examples list the 42 non-deprecated ODRL 2.2 Action terms.

LeftOperand.description: Reference to an ODRL LeftOperand left operand. Open: any IRI is accepted, so ODRL profile terms (e.g. cdifa1:) validate; the examples list the 32 non-deprecated ODRL 2.2 LeftOperand terms.

Operator.description: Reference to an ODRL Operator operator. Open: any IRI is accepted, so ODRL profile terms (e.g. cdifa1:) validate; the examples list the 12 non-deprecated ODRL 2.2 Operator terms.

RightOperand.description: Reference to an ODRL RightOperand right operand. Open: any IRI is accepted, so ODRL profile terms (e.g. cdifa1:) validate; the examples list the 1 non-deprecated ODRL 2.2 RightOperand terms. Most right operands are literals or value objects, not terms; this is for the few that are IRIs.

ConflictTerm.description: Strategy for resolving conflicts between permissions and prohibitions (odrl:conflict). Closed: ODRL defines exactly these three.

cdif.bbr.metadata.odrlProperties.odrlAss.title: ODRL Asset
cdif.bbr.metadata.odrlProperties.odrlAss.description: An ODRL 2.2 Asset (https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-model/#asset) or AssetCollection (https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-model/#asset-collection): the resource a rule applies to. In CDIF this is normally a distribution or data service, identified by its IRI. An AssetCollection groups assets: either the collection itself, identified by @id, or a subset of one, where odrl:source names the collection and odrl:refinement narrows it (e.g. the CSV distributions of a dataset).

@context.description: JSON-LD namespace prefixes for ODRL properties.

odrl:partOf.description: AssetCollections this asset is a member of.

AssetCollection.description: Per ODRL, a refined collection is identified through odrl:source, so odrl:refinement requires odrl:source.

odrl:source.description: The collection this one is drawn from.

odrl:refinement.description: Constraints selecting the members of odrl:source that belong to this collection.

cdif.bbr.metadata.odrlProperties.odrlPar.title: ODRL Party
cdif.bbr.metadata.odrlProperties.odrlPar.description: An ODRL 2.2 Party (https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-model/#party) or PartyCollection (https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-model/#party-collection): who takes a role (assigner, assignee) in a rule. A Party is a person, organization or agent identified by its IRI. A PartyCollection is a group of parties: either the collection itself, identified by @id, or a subset of one, where odrl:source names the collection and odrl:refinement narrows it (e.g. registered users located in the UK).

@context.description: JSON-LD namespace prefixes for ODRL and schema.org properties.

Party.description: Typed odrl:Party, schema:Person or schema:Organization. ODRL declares odrl:Party a subclass of schema:Person or schema:Organization (among FOAF and vCard classes), and gives odrl:assigner and odrl:assignee the range odrl:Party, so a schema.org-typed node in those roles is an odrl:Party without saying so. A schema:Person is validated by the person block and a schema:Organization by the organization block. A person may also carry odrl:Party; an organization may not, because the organization block only accepts schema.org organization types in @type.

PartyCollection.description: Per ODRL, a refined collection is identified through odrl:source, so odrl:refinement requires odrl:source.

odrl:source.description: The collection this one is drawn from.

odrl:refinement.description: Constraints selecting the members of odrl:source that belong to this collection.

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.pe.description: schema for cdif profile of schema.org/Person

schema:name.description: string label for person that is meaningful for human users, should format consistently. Recommend 'Family Name, Given name' format.

schema:description.description: additional information about the agent or their relation to the described resource

schema:alternateName.description: other labels by which the person might be known

schema:affiliation.description: if affiliation is present, value must be a schema:Organization.

schema:contactPoint.description: An email address or a contact web page (a form, an issue tracker), or both; at least one is required. Schema.org also allows telephone and postal contacts. A URL-only contact is ordinary in DCAT (a vcard:Kind with only vcard:hasURL), so requiring email made such records invalid.

schema:name.description: string label for organization that is meaningful for human users

schema:alternateName.description: other labels by which the organization might be known

schema:description.description: additional information about the agent or their relation to the described resource

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.id.description:
Properties for a schema.org identifier (schema:PropertyValue pattern).
**Union-type policy:** In CDIF profile UML models an attribute typed as
schema:Identifier / schema:PropertyValue is represented by a single attribute
of that class type. The JSON Schema implementation permits the property value
to be EITHER a plain string (interpreted as the bare identifier value) OR a
full schema:PropertyValue object (with explicit @type, propertyID, value).
Consumers should accept either form.

schema:propertyID.description: In this context for the schema:PropertyValue, this field is an identifier for the identifier schema, e.g. DOI, ARK.  Get values from https://registry.identifiers.org/registry/ for interoperability. URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}) so they participate in RDF entailment; free-label strings remain valid as strings.

schema:url.description: web-resolveable string for the identifier; host name part is location of a resolver that will return some representation for the given identifier value. E.g. https://doi.org/10.5066/F7VX0DMQ

cdif.bbr.metadata.cdifDataType.cdifConce.title: CDIF Concept-or-Term-or-String
cdif.bbr.metadata.cdifDataType.cdifConce.description: Shared shape for a CDIF property that carries either a controlled-vocabulary value or a bare string label. Wraps cdifConceptOrTerm (SKOS-concept @id-ref, schema:DefinedTerm, or inline cdif:Concept) with a plain-string alternative used for legacy or single-word labels not yet bound to a vocabulary.

A SKOS concept identified by URI, a schema:DefinedTerm, or an inline cdif:Concept. Shared shape used wherever a CDIF property carries either a controlled-vocabulary reference or an inline concept definition.

anyOf.description: reference to a skos concept for the data type

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.de.description:
schema.org Defined Term schema.

**Union-type policy:** In CDIF profile UML models an attribute typed as
schema:DefinedTerm is represented by a single attribute of that class type.
The JSON Schema implementation permits the property value to be EITHER a
plain string (interpreted as schema:name or schema:termCode in the default
vocabulary) OR a full schema:DefinedTerm object (with explicit @type, name,
identifier, termCode, inDefinedTermSet). Consumers should accept either form.

Note that this differs from the cdif Concept policy: a Concept (skos:Concept)
in CDIF profiles MUST be a controlled-vocabulary entry (object form or
@id-reference) — plain strings are not permitted for Concept-typed values
because vocabulary identity cannot be recovered from an unscoped label.

schema:name.description: text label for the term that is useful to human user

schema:inDefinedTermSet.description: The controlled vocabulary responsible for this keyword, as EITHER a plain URI string identifying the vocabulary, OR an object reference ({"@id": "<uri>"}) to a vocabulary defined elsewhere in the document. Both forms are already in use across CDIF profiles and downstream ADA building blocks; permitting only the string form made the object form - the natural JSON-LD spelling of a reference - invalid, while this class's own union-type policy above explicitly anticipates both.

schema:termCode.description: A representative code for this keyword in the controlled vocabulary. Analogous to skos:Notation

cdif.bbr.metadata.skosProperties.skosCon.title: SKOS Concept
cdif.bbr.metadata.skosProperties.skosCon.description: JSON Schema for a SKOS Concept in JSON-LD form. A unit of thought within a concept scheme. Supports labels (prefLabel, altLabel, hiddenLabel), notations, hierarchical relations (broader/narrower), associative relations (related), cross-scheme mapping properties, scheme membership, and documentary notes. Based on the W3C SKOS Reference (https://www.w3.org/TR/skos-reference/).

@context.description: JSON-LD context declaring the skos namespace prefix. May be a single object or an array of strings and objects.

skos:prefLabel.description: Preferred lexical label for this concept. A single string, a single language-tagged value, or an array of language-tagged values. Each language should appear at most once.

skos:notation.description: Classification code for this concept within a scheme (a single notation string, consistent with CdifCodelistConcept).

skos:definition.description: Formal explanation of the meaning of this concept.

skos:scopeNote.description: Note clarifying meaning and/or intended use.

skos:historyNote.description: Note about past state or use.

skos:inScheme.description: Concept scheme(s) this concept belongs to.

skos:topConceptOf.description: Concept scheme(s) for which this is a top concept.

skos:broader.description: Broader (parent) concepts in the hierarchy. Items are inline concept objects or @id references.

skos:narrower.description: Narrower (child) concepts in the hierarchy. Items are inline concept objects or @id references.

ConceptRef.description: A reference to a SKOS Concept by URI.

LanguageTaggedValue.description: An RDF literal value with a language tag, serialized as a JSON-LD value object.

@language.description: BCP 47 language tag (e.g. en, fr, de).

title: CDIF Access
description:
Profile module for machine-actionable access and usage conditions, expressed as ODRL Offer policies (odrlProperties/odrlOffer). Marks the catalog record as conformant to the CDIF access spec and requires at least one policy, attached in either of two places:
- on a schema:distribution item, as odrl:hasPolicy: the preferred place,
  because distributions of one dataset can carry different conditions
  (cdifbook data_access, "Connecting CDIF and ODRL"). The Offer may be
  inline or an {@id} reference.

- on the Dataset, as an {@id} reference in schema:conditionsOfAccess to
  a policy published elsewhere. Only a reference: cdifCore types the
  items of that property as string, {@id} or a CreativeWork link, and an
  inline Offer matches none of them, so it would fail any composite that
  includes cdifCore.

This module adds constraints only; it does not change cdifCore's schema:distribution anyOf [DataDownload, WebAPI]. Draft; OPEN QUESTIONS are marked "OPEN:".

@context.description: Additional JSON-LD namespace prefixes for access properties.

dcterms:conformsTo.description: OPEN: https://w3id.org/cdif/access/1.1 is not minted. 1.1 follows the other CDIF modules; a new profile might start at 1.0 instead.

schema:conditionsOfAccess.description: Item shape comes from cdifCore. In a CDIF Access record, an {@id} item here should be the uid of an ODRL Offer; JSON Schema cannot tell that reference from any other (a SHACL rule would have to).

odrl:hasPolicy.description: ODRL policies governing access to and use of this distribution. OPEN: the book argues against dataset-level policies, so odrl:hasPolicy is not declared on the Dataset; confirm.
